query: What signals suggest a goal will be highly achieved?

per_column.name: baseline_reference_clarity
per_column.rationale: Whether a goal states an explicit baseline/comparison is a plausible signal for achievability and gives a real grouping axis. Values are well-grounded: samples with '78% to 90%' or 'compared to last quarter' correctly get explicit; the categorisation reads the source soundly.

per_column.name: timeline_explicitness
per_column.rationale: Timeline specificity is a reasonable achievement signal and offers a distinct axis. Grounding is mostly sound, though 'next fiscal year' and 'upcoming year' are labelled fiscal_period while 'by end of Q4' is specific_date—slight inconsistency but defensible readings of the text.

per_column.name: goal_category
per_column.rationale: Values are directly grounded (they mirror the description and the original 'category' column). But this largely duplicates the existing 'category' column, so it adds little new analytical leverage.

per_column.name: intervention_specificity
per_column.rationale: Type of intervention is a genuine new axis for modelling achievement. Grounded generally, but some labels are debatable—'increase premium subscriptions' tagged strategic_direction while similar concrete goals get process_improvement; borderline but not invented.

per_column.name: implementation_scope
per_column.rationale: Single vs multi-faceted scope is a usable signal. Grounding is reasonable (goals naming two levers get multi_faceted), though single_lever vs multi_faceted judgements can be somewhat subjective. Overlaps conceptually with supporting_mechanism_depth.

per_column.name: supporting_mechanism_depth
per_column.rationale: Its two-value single-vs-multiple-lever distinction is largely a restatement of implementation_scope, adding little independent leverage. Also note inconsistency: the Employee Engagement sample is multi_faceted in scope but single_primary_lever here.

per_column.name: execution_explicitness
per_column.rationale: Whether a named/tested program is cited is a plausible achievement signal and a distinct axis. Grounding is sound: 'Employee Engagement Program' -> explicit_program_name; goals lacking named methods -> vague_intent.

per_column.name: metric_goal_fit
per_column.rationale: Alignment between the 'metric' column and the goal is a strong achievement signal and directly analysable. Well grounded: mismatches like customer-satisfaction goal with 'Expense Ratio' metric are correctly flagged metric_mismatched.

per_column.name: resource_or_investment_mention
per_column.rationale: Presence of resource/investment language is a reasonable signal, but grounding is questionable: the first sample about 'optimize duplicated resources' is marked True as a resource mention, which conflates a cost lever with an actual resource/investment commitment—an over-reading.

judge.rationale: Most added columns provide genuine, distinct axes (metric_goal_fit, baseline clarity, timeline explicitness, intervention/execution specificity) that materially help model what drives high goal achievement, and their values are largely sound readings of the description text. Weaknesses: goal_category duplicates the existing 'category' column, supporting_mechanism_depth largely restates implementation_scope, and resource_or_investment_mention shows some over-reading of the source. Overall grounding is strong with a few debatable/inconsistent labels.
